semantically_equivalent_models.justification: FactorNet is related to matrix factorization as both involve the decomposition of matrices, typically used in recommender systems. While "matrix factorization" refers to the general technique, "factornet" specifically implements this concept, thus they are semantically equivalent.
Mat-2d is an application of matrix factorization in two dimensions, closely related to the general concept of matrix factorization.

parent_models.justification: Hidden Interaction Tensor Factorization is a broader model that extends matrix factorization to tensor factorization, making it a parent model.
This model builds on hidden interaction tensor factorization, further generalizing matrix factorization to collective contexts, thus also being a parent model.

closest_parent_model.justification: Among the parent models, hidden interaction tensor factorization is closest to simple matrix factorization, as it involves factorization of higher dimensional arrays (tensors) similar to matrices, without additional layers of complexity as in "collective" approaches.

child_models.justification: Movie recommender systems often utilize matrix factorization techniques to predict user preferences, making it a child model of matrix factorization.

closest_child_model.justification: Among child models, movie recommender is indeed the closest because it directly utilizes matrix factorization as a core technique for its predictive functionalities.

sibling_models.justification: Although broader, collective hidden interaction tensor factorization shares a close conceptual space with the hidden interaction tensor factorization, which is a direct parent of matrix factorization. Thus, it can be considered a sibling in the hierarchical model space.

closest_sibling_model.justification: Out of the potential siblings, collective hidden interaction tensor factorization is the closest sibling, as it extends the concept of tensor factorization more similar to hidden interaction tensor factorization.

unrelated_models.justification: Linear Discriminant Analysis is primarily a classification technique and unlike matrix factorization, does not decompose matrices or tensors.
Like LDA, this technique focuses on maximizing variance for classification purposes and does not involve matrix decomposition.
Gradient boosting is an ensemble learning technique and does not involve matrix or tensor factorization.
This is a classification model related to LDA and does not involve matrix decomposition.
Eigenoptions is a method related to reinforcement learning and hierarchical decomposition, disconnected from the area of matrix factorization.
SVMRank involves ranking and support vector machines, unrelated to matrix decomposition.
Linear classifiers represent data linearly, unrelated to the factorization process.
Mixture-of-experts is a model ensembling strategy, not involving matrix or tensor decomposition.
K-means clustering is a clustering algorithm that does not involve matrix or tensor decomposition.
Inner-lasso is related to regularization techniques in linear models, disjoint from matrix factorization.
This is a hierarchical clustering technique, unrelated to the decomposition involved in matrix factorization.
This method is mainly an optimization technique, not pertaining to factorization.
Vector quantization is about quantization in high-dimensional space, different from matrix factorization.
This is related to graph-based learning and not matrix factorization.
Hierarchical clustering involves clustering rather than matrix or tensor factorization.
